comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
DB99F260DFE50131E7B268A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

DB99AC40DFE50131E7B168A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

DBED2A40DFE50131E84C68A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

DBECE170DFE50131E84B68A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

DBEC8860DFE50131E84A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

DBEC19C0DFE50131E84968A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

DBEBD010DFE50131E84868A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

DBEB89D0DFE50131E84768A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

DBEB4850DFE50131E84668A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

DBEB0440DFE50131E84568A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

DBEAC1D0DFE50131E84468A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

DBEA7810DFE50131E84368A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100
For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.
DBE9E340DFE50131E84168A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

DBE9A030DFE50131E84068A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

DBE96140DFE50131E83F68A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

DBE8D1B0DFE50131E83D68A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

DBE87760DFE50131E83C68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

DBE82F10DFE50131E83B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

DBE7D5E0DFE50131E83A68A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

DBE788A0DFE50131E83968A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

DBE73C40DFE50131E83868A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

DBE6F810DFE50131E83768A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

DBE699F0DFE50131E83668A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

DBE63060DFE50131E83568A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

DBE5E9D0DFE50131E83468A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

DBE5A5B0DFE50131E83368A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

DBE55F70DFE50131E83268A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

DBE43AF0DFE50131E82E68A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

DBE3F820DFE50131E82D68A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.
comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

DBE50D90DFE50131E83168A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
comments: Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.

DBE4BB70DFE50131E83068A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

DBE47CE0DFE50131E82F68A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

DBE31B10DFE50131E82A68A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

DBE2CF20DFE50131E82968A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

DBE28480DFE50131E82868A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

DBE23670DFE50131E82768A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
comments: A range of algorithms may be used.

DBE1F280DFE50131E82668A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

DBE19EC0DFE50131E82568A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.
comments: For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.

DBE15300DFE50131E82468A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
comments: This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

DBE10E10DFE50131E82368A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

DBE0C5E0DFE50131E82268A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

DBDF9C00DFE50131E81E68A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

DBDF5930DFE50131E81D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

DBDF16E0DFE50131E81C68A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

DBDE4420DFE50131E81968A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

DBDBE5C0DFE50131E81268A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

DBDB30A0DFE50131E81068A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

D7A7A230DFE50131DFAC68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

D7A74E40DFE50131DFAB68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D7A69990DFE50131DFA968A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

D7A641A0DFE50131DFA868A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

D7A5E9C0DFE50131DFA768A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another, and show the relationships among experiences and events.

D7A58BF0DFE50131DFA668A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

D7A534C0DFE50131DFA568A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

D7A4CD50DFE50131DFA468A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

D7A48340DFE50131DFA368A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

D7A437B0DFE50131DFA268A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

D7A3E390DFE50131DFA168A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

D7A38EA0DFE50131DFA068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

D7A33D10DFE50131DF9F68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

D7A2C670DFE50131DF9E68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

D7A264C0DFE50131DF9D68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

D7A20D40DFE50131DF9C68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

D7A1AC40DFE50131DF9B68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

D7A162D0DFE50131DF9A68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

D7A11840DFE50131DF9968A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

D7A0CCA0DFE50131DF9868A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

D7A08040DFE50131DF9768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

D79F83F0DFE50131DF9468A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

D79EDE70DFE50131DF9268A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D79E8120DFE50131DF9168A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

D79E1570DFE50131DF9068A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

D79DC8D0DFE50131DF8F68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D79D74C0DFE50131DF8E68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

D79CFA80DFE50131DF8D68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

D79C9980DFE50131DF8C68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D79BEBB0DFE50131DF8A68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

D79B9CE0DFE50131DF8968A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

D79B4C10DFE50131DF8868A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

D79AA8F0DFE50131DF8668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

D79A4380DFE50131DF8568A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D799F3D0DFE50131DF8468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D7999E30DFE50131DF8368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

D79947A0DFE50131DF8268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

D798EE30DFE50131DF8168A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

D7984490DFE50131DF7F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

D797F470DFE50131DF7E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

D7978F70DFE50131DF7D68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

D796D4D0DFE50131DF7B68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

D7967FA0DFE50131DF7A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

D79632A0DFE50131DF7968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

D7959110DFE50131DF7768A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

D79537E0DFE50131DF7668A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D794BFF0DFE50131DF7568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D7945F20DFE50131DF7468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

D793FE30DFE50131DF7368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

D79393E0DFE50131DF7268A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

D792E6B0DFE50131DF7068A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

D79287D0DFE50131DF6F68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

D79233A0DFE50131DF6E68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

D79152D0DFE50131DF6C68A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

D79107D0DFE50131DF6B68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

D790BCE0DFE50131DF6A68A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

D79026B0DFE50131DF6868A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

D78FD890DFE50131DF6768A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D78F7690DFE50131DF6668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D78F2860DFE50131DF6568A86D17958E.description: Analyze a case in which two or more texts provide conflicting information on the same topic and identify where the texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretation.

D78ED950DFE50131DF6468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

D78E8720DFE50131DF6368A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different mediums (e.g., print or digital text, video, multimedia) to present a particular topic or idea.

D78DD0D0DFE50131DF6168A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author acknowledges and responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

D78D7BB0DFE50131DF6068A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.

D78D21F0DFE50131DF5F68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

D78C7D70DFE50131DF5D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events (e.g., through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

D78C2620DFE50131DF5C68A86D17958E.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary of the text.

D75DA770DFE50131DF5B68A86D17958E.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

D75C9CB0DFE50131DF5868A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D75C4EA0DFE50131DF5768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D75BAB00DFE50131DF5568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new.

D75B5200DFE50131DF5468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

D75ABB20DFE50131DF5268A86D17958E.description: Analyze how differences in the points of view of the characters and the audience or reader (e.g., created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor.

D75A6830DFE50131DF5168A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the structure of two or more texts and analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to its meaning and style.

D75A1590DFE50131DF5068A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

D75941C0DFE50131DF4E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

D758F0C0DFE50131DF4D68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot; provide an objective summary of the text.

D758A180DFE50131DF4C68A86D17958E.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

D75780E0DFE50131DF4968A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

D7573300DFE50131DF4868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D756E400DFE50131DF4768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

D75693D0DFE50131DF4668A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

D7563B40DFE50131DF4568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

D7558BD0DFE50131DF4368A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

D75539C0DFE50131DF4268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

D754DE80DFE50131DF4168A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

D75405E0DFE50131DF3F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

D753AD40DFE50131DF3E68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

D7535570DFE50131DF3D68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

D752ABE0DFE50131DF3B68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Kentucky Core Academic Standards - English Language Arts

D5DB2360DFE50131DC5868A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that night we went looking for them).

D5DACBD0DFE50131DC5768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

D5DA79B0DFE50131DC5668A86D17958E.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are friendly or helpful).

D5DA2660DFE50131DC5568A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

D5D9DD70DFE50131DC5468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

D5D99240DFE50131DC5368A86D17958E.description: Use glossaries or beginning dictionaries, both print and digital, to determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

D5D93C40DFE50131DC5268A86D17958E.description: Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g., company, companion).

D5D8DC50DFE50131DC5168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word (e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

D5D88C90DFE50131DC5068A86D17958E.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

D5D82530DFE50131DC4F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning word and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

D5D79140DFE50131DC4D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard English.

D5D74770DFE50131DC4C68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

D5D6F570DFE50131DC4B68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D5D64D40DFE50131DC4968A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, as needed to check and correct spellings.

D5D5F910DFE50131DC4868A86D17958E.description: Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

D5D5A0F0DFE50131DC4768A86D17958E.description: Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

D5D50FC0DFE50131DC4568A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

D5D42020DFE50131DC4268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D5D3CFE0DFE50131DC4168A86D17958E.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

D5D30160DFE50131DC3F68A86D17958E.description: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.

D5D26310DFE50131DC3D68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

D5D21520DFE50131DC3C68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

D5D17550DFE50131DC3A68A86D17958E.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

D5D119F0DFE50131DC3968A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their functions in particular sentences.

D5D0BAB0DFE50131DC3868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D5CFCDF0DFE50131DC3568A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

D5CF7F10DFE50131DC3468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D5CF28A0DFE50131DC3368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

D5CE9220DFE50131DC3168A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

D5CDF1F0DFE50131DC2F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D5CD9A90DFE50131DC2E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D5CD0610DFE50131DC2C68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

D5CCBF30DFE50131DC2B68A86D17958E.description: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.

D5CC75A0DFE50131DC2A68A86D17958E.description: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.

D5CC2D00DFE50131DC2968A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

D5CB8FD0DFE50131DC2768A86D17958E.description: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.

D5CB4550DFE50131DC2668A86D17958E.description: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D5CAFB90DFE50131DC2568A86D17958E.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

D5CAAEB0DFE50131DC2468A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.

D5CA6220DFE50131DC2368A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

D5CA10B0DFE50131DC2268A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

D5C9B030DFE50131DC2168A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

D5C8A4F0DFE50131DC1E68A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

D5C84EB0DFE50131DC1D68A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

D5C7D740DFE50131DC1C68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D5C739F0DFE50131DC1A68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

D5C6EF50DFE50131DC1968A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D5C6A030DFE50131DC1868A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

D5C60560DFE50131DC1668A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

D5C5BD10DFE50131DC1568A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

D5C4D610DFE50131DC1268A86D17958E.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

D5C47680DFE50131DC1168A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

D5C424E0DFE50131DC1068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D5C3CDC0DFE50131DC0F68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

D5C37ED0DFE50131DC0E68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

D5C32D10DFE50131DC0D68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.

document.title: Kentucky Core Academic Standards - English Language Arts

D62B25E0DFE50131DCFB68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

D62AD8C0DFE50131DCFA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

D62A83F0DFE50131DCF968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

D62A2D20DFE50131DCF868A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

D629C910DFE50131DCF768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D62970D0DFE50131DCF668A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

D62901E0DFE50131DCF568A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

D628A190DFE50131DCF468A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

D6285710DFE50131DCF368A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

D627B4C0DFE50131DCF168A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

D6271C70DFE50131DCEF68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

D626CFF0DFE50131DCEE68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

D62630F0DFE50131DCEC68A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

D625CD80DFE50131DCEB68A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

D6257980DFE50131DCEA68A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

D624CA20DFE50131DCE868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D6247A40DFE50131DCE768A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

D6242930DFE50131DCE668A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

D6237630DFE50131DCE468A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

D6232490DFE50131DCE368A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

D622DD70DFE50131DCE268A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

D6229260DFE50131DCE168A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

D6224240DFE50131DCE068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D6215AF0DFE50131DCDD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

D62110D0DFE50131DCDC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

D620C540DFE50131DCDB68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

D6200F60DFE50131DCD968A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

D61F6B70DFE50131DCD768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

D61F1DE0DFE50131DCD668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

D61E8820DFE50131DCD468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

D61E2DA0DFE50131DCD368A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

D61DD260DFE50131DCD268A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

D619B950DFE50131DCC668A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

D6196F90DFE50131DCC568A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

D6192490DFE50131DCC468A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D6187B80DFE50131DCC268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

D6180EF0DFE50131DCC168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

D617B030DFE50131DCC068A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

B881C70D892D49928E2262B74273D106.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

B69CBF4594DF421F808F3FDF7D64C504.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

22038B0CE3FE4EA68BC42917441AD9FB.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

827E83C1A8E7430993838CFCF758950A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

D6609720DFE50131DD5368A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

D6604E50DFE50131DD5268A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

D6600560DFE50131DD5168A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

D65FB600DFE50131DD5068A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

D65F61A0DFE50131DD4F68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

D65F15B0DFE50131DD4E68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented

D65ECDC0DFE50131DD4D68A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

D65E8620DFE50131DD4C68A86D17958E.description: Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., in contrast, especially).

D65E3D60DFE50131DD4B68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples related to the topic.

D65DF1B0DFE50131DD4A68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, provide a general observation and focus, and group related information logically; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

D65D8040DFE50131DD4968A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

D65D2D50DFE50131DD4868A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

D65CD8F0DFE50131DD4768A86D17958E.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

D65C8D80DFE50131DD4668A86D17958E.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

D65C40C0DFE50131DD4568A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which ideas are logically grouped to support the writer's purpose.

D65BF010DFE50131DD4468A86D17958E.description: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information

D65AD190DFE50131DD4168A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

D65A2D60DFE50131DD3F68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

D659D130DFE50131DD3E68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

D65984D0DFE50131DD3D68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

D6593860DFE50131DD3C68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

D658E990DFE50131DD3B68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

D65892F0DFE50131DD3A68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

D6583860DFE50131DD3968A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D6578BA0DFE50131DD3768A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

D65740E0DFE50131DD3668A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

D656EF70DFE50131DD3568A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

D6565D40DFE50131DD3368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

D65610D0DFE50131DD3268A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

D655AC20DFE50131DD3168A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

D6554740DFE50131DD3068A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

D654F520DFE50131DD2F68A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

D65463C0DFE50131DD2D68A86D17958E.description: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes) to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.

D65416A0DFE50131DD2C68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

D65308F0DFE50131DD2968A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D6529CD0DFE50131DD2868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D6522FF0DFE50131DD2768A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

D651E610DFE50131DD2668A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

D6519620DFE50131DD2568A86D17958E.description: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.

D650EF70DFE50131DD2368A86D17958E.description: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.

D6509E60DFE50131DD2268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.

D6504A40DFE50131DD2168A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

D64F7A70DFE50131DD1F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.

D64F33A0DFE50131DD1E68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.

D64EEB20DFE50131DD1D68A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

D64E0DF0DFE50131DD1A68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the high end of the grades 4—5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D64DB340DFE50131DD1968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D64D13C0DFE50131DD1768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and topics.

D64CCAE0DFE50131DD1668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text (e.g., graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

D64C2E30DFE50131DD1468A86D17958E.description: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.

D64BCBB0DFE50131DD1368A86D17958E.description: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.

D64B7170DFE50131DD1268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.

D64AC0E0DFE50131DD1068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

D64A64F0DFE50131DD0F68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.

D649FAF0DFE50131DD0E68A86D17958E.description: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

D64922C0DFE50131DD0B68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

D648DAC0DFE50131DD0A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D6488E20DFE50131DD0968A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

D6483B00DFE50131DD0868A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

D647EF10DFE50131DD0768A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

D6475930DFE50131DD0568A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

D6470CC0DFE50131DD0468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

D646BD50DFE50131DD0368A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

D6461970DFE50131DD0168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

D645CCF0DFE50131DD0068A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

D64581D0DFE50131DCFF68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.
